cases.explain: Поезд is the grammatical subject of тронулся (started moving), so it is in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Он говорил обо всем без всякой ___и.
cases.translation: He talked about everything without any real need to.
cases.explain: The preposition без (without) governs the genitive case.

cases.translation: Reckoning by the artillery officer's years (age).
cases.explain: The preposition по (by) governs the dative case (here plural).

cases.translation: What had prompted him to go to Serbia.
cases.explain: В (to) with a verb of motion governs the accusative case.

cases.translation: "I am a retired cadet," he said.
cases.explain: The instrumental case is used for the predicate noun describing his former role — 'I was a cadet.'

cases.translation: A middle-aged officer in an Austrian military jersey.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in/wearing) governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Простившись с княгиней, Сергей Иванович вместе с подошедшим Котовасовым вошел в битком набитый вагон и поезд тронулся.
reading.question: What happens as Sergei Ivanovich and Katavasov board the train?
options: They bid farewell to the princess, board a packed carriage, and the train departs
They are seated alone in first class
reading.correct: They bid farewell to the princess, board a packed carriage, and the train departs
reading.explain: After saying goodbye to the princess, they board a crammed carriage and the train sets off.

reading.ru: На Царицынской станции поезд был встречен стройным хором молодых людей, певших «Слався».
reading.question: How was the train greeted at the Tsaritsyno station?
options: By a harmonious choir of young people singing "Slavsya"
reading.correct: By a harmonious choir of young people singing "Slavsya"
reading.explain: At the Tsaritsyno station the train was met by a well-tuned choir of young people singing "Slavsya."

reading.ru: Он столько имел дел с добровольцами, что уже знал их общий тип, и это не интересовало его.
reading.question: Why did the volunteers not particularly interest Sergei Ivanovich?
options: Because he had dealt with so many volunteers he already knew their general type
Because he disapproved of the war
Because he was too tired to notice them
Because he did not speak their language
reading.correct: Because he had dealt with so many volunteers he already knew their general type
reading.explain: The text explains he had had so much to do with volunteers that he already knew their general type, so it no longer interested him.

reading.ru: Вступив в разговор с юношей, Котовасов узнал, что это был богатый московский купец, промотавший большое состояние до 22 лет.
reading.question: What did Katavasov learn about the young man he spoke with?
options: That he was a rich Moscow merchant who had squandered a large fortune by age 22
That he was a foreign spy
That he was a decorated general
reading.correct: That he was a rich Moscow merchant who had squandered a large fortune by age 22
reading.explain: Katavasov learns the young man was a wealthy Moscow merchant who had squandered a large fortune before turning 22.

reading.ru: Третий артиллерист, напротив, очень понравился Котовасову.
reading.question: Which volunteer did Katavasov like the most?
options: The old man in the military coat
reading.explain: The text states the third man, the artillery officer, was, on the contrary, very much liked by Katavasov.

reading.ru: «Да что ж, все едут. Надо тоже помочь и сербам. Жалко».
reading.question: How does the modest artilleryman explain his reason for going to Serbia?
options: He says everyone is going, and out of pity he must help the Serbs too
He says he was ordered to go
He says he wants to escape debt
reading.correct: He says everyone is going, and out of pity he must help the Serbs too
reading.explain: He modestly answers that everyone is going, that the Serbs need help too, and that it is a pitiable situation.

reading.ru: Он знал, что такое военный человек, и по виду и разговору этих господ, по ухорству, с которым они прикладывались к фляжке дорогой, он считал их за плохих военных.
reading.question: What did the old man traveling in a military coat conclude about the volunteers?
options: That, judging by their appearance and manner with the flask, they were poor soldiers
That they were too young to serve
reading.correct: That, judging by their appearance and manner with the flask, they were poor soldiers
reading.explain: Knowing what a real military man was like, and seeing how readily they took to the flask on the road, he judged them to be poor soldiers.

reading.ru: Котовасов, войдя в свой вагон, невольно кривя душой рассказал Сергею Ивановичу свои наблюдения над добровольцами, из которых оказывалось, что они были отличные ребята.
reading.question: What did Katavasov report to Sergei Ivanovich about the volunteers, despite his private doubts?
options: That, against his true feelings, he said they were excellent fellows
That he refused to discuss them
That he wanted to join them
reading.correct: That, against his true feelings, he said they were excellent fellows
reading.explain: Returning to his own carriage, Katavasov, not quite honestly, told Sergei Ivanovich his observations made the volunteers out to be excellent fellows.

reading.ru: Но все это было уже гораздо слабее и меньше, чем в Москве.
reading.question: How did the reception for volunteers at the large provincial city compare to Moscow's?
options: It was much weaker and smaller than in Moscow
It was even grander than in Moscow
There was no reception at all
reading.correct: It was much weaker and smaller than in Moscow
reading.explain: The text notes that all of this was already much weaker and smaller than it had been in Moscow.
